Classroom 2-B / The One Who Kept Asking — Trinity General School, Classroom 2-B

Status: Active — student, Classroom 2-B; asked the questions that produced the SCHALE disclosure and the Equestrian liaison admission

Asa Hanko is the student the advisor had to look twice at to place, and the one who did the most damage to his lesson plan. Hanko asked what SCHALE was, asked what the acronym actually meant, asked what Sectors 7 through 12 were, asked about the Equestrian liaison seen walking the school, and asked whether the class would be armed. Every significant disclosure in the filing exists because Hanko would not let a term pass unexplained.

Evidence

  • Silver Tongue — “He confirmed a Canterlot diplomatic programme, confirmed it was supposed to be quiet, and admitted someone had dropped the ball on security protocols.”

Status: Active — student, Classroom 2-B; founding member of the outfit-design alliance formed during the advisor's first roll call

Airi sits by the window, keeps chocolate in her desk drawer, and is the social connective tissue of Classroom 2-B. She welcomed the new advisor, briefed the newcomer on what was normal, gave the advisor a chocolate mint, then carried another one to the back of the room for the student nobody else was talking to. Her enthusiasm is constant and occasionally deafening, and it is also the only thing in the room that reliably crosses the seating politics.

Advisor to Classroom 2-B / SCHALE Liaison — Trinity General School (advisor); SCHALE

Status: Active — newly assigned advisor to Classroom 2-B at Trinity General School; disclosed the class's SCHALE attachment during his first roll call and opened an internal query into the Equestrian liaison security breach

Sensei is the advisor assigned to Classroom 2-B, and the first adult in this campaign's record to tell the students what they are actually enrolled in. He introduced himself as the glue holding the operation together, ran a roll call, and — when a student asked a direct question — confirmed that the class is attached to SCHALE operations. He is not the students' friend and does not try to be. He is the person who answers the question. His method is volume and posture rather than authority he actually possesses. He defused a student's declaration of lordship by thanking him for his cooperation. He is, on the evidence of one session, a man who has run this room before and expects to run it again.

Evidence

  • Dagger — “Advisor to Classroom 2-B / SCHALE Liaison”
  • Silver Tongue — “He confirmed a diplomatic programme with Canterlot, confirmed it was meant to be quiet, and said that students seeing it meant someone dropped the ball on security protocols.”

That admission is the most valuable thing anyone says: he has been at Trinity for years and nobody ever explained SCHALE to him, which reframes the entire disclosure from a briefing into an indictment.

Supplementary Student / The Corner Desk — Trinity General School, Classroom 2-B

Status: Active — student, Classroom 2-B; classified within the school system as a supplementary student, a designation she named aloud and objected to

Azusa sits in the far corner, as far from everyone else as a desk allows, with her posture straight, her pen aligned parallel to her notebook's edge, and her expression unreadable. She answers roll call with a nod barely large enough to register. She is also the only student in the room who reacted to the word SCHALE with something other than excitement, because she is the only one who has been on the receiving end of it.

Evidence

  • Fists — “Supplementary Student / The Corner Desk”
  • Silver Tongue — “While the rest of the room negotiated outfits, Azusa asked the question underneath the whole session, quietly, to nobody: "The question is whether SCHALE actually works.”
  • Keen Records — “Azusa's eyes sharpened, and the record describes it precisely: like a blade being drawn from a sheath so smooth you'd miss it if you blinked.”
